## Problem 1

### Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(patchwork)

set.seed(127)
```

## Birthdays

```{r}
birthday_repeated = function(n) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  length(unique(birthdays)) < n
}

birthday_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    number_of_people = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    repeated = map_lgl(number_of_people, birthday_repeated)
  )

birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(number_of_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = number_of_people, y = prob_of_repeat)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line()
```

## Problem 2

### Combining experimental and control data; tidying data

```{r}
long_study_df =
  tibble(
    file_path = c(list.files("data",full.names = TRUE))
  )

subjects_df =
  long_study_df |> 
  mutate(
    filename = basename(file_path),
    subject_id = str_remove(filename, "\\.csv$"),
    arm = if_else(str_starts(filename, "con"), "control", "experimental"),
    data = map(file_path, ~ read_csv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE))
  ) |> 
  unnest(data) |> 
   pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("week_"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "week_",
    values_to = "observation"
  ) |> 
  mutate(week = as.numeric(week)) |> 
  select(subject_id, arm, week, observation)
```

### Spaghetti plot

```{r}
subjects_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = observation, color = arm)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = subject_id)) +
  geom_point()
```

* The control arm had overall less observations compared to the experimental arm The experimental arm observations increased over time while the control arm remained relatively level.

## Problem 3

### mu = 0

```{r}
mean_sd = function(n = 30, mu = 0, sigma = 5) {
  
  sim_df = 
    tibble(
      x = rnorm(n = n, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
    )
  
  sim_df |> 
    summarize(
      results = list(t.test(x, mu = 0) |> broom::tidy())) |> 
    unnest(results)
}

output = vector("list", length = 5000)

for (i in 1:5000){
   output[[i]] = mean_sd()
}

output |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
  select(estimate, p.value)
```

### mu = 1:6

```{r}
all_outputs = vector("list", length = 6)

for (m in 1:6) {
  
  output = vector("list", length = 5000)
  
  for (i in 1:5000) {
    output[[i]] = mean_sd(mu = m)
  }
  
  all_outputs[[m]] = output |> 
    bind_rows() |> 
    select(estimate, p.value) |> 
    mutate(true_mu = m)
}

true_sim_df = bind_rows(all_outputs)
```

### mu vs power

```{r}
true_sim_df |> 
  group_by(true_mu) |> 
  summarize(
    power = mean(p.value < 0.05), .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = true_mu, y = power)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()
```

* effect size: (mu - mu-null/sigma); mu = 1:6, mu-null = 0, sigma = 5
* As effect size increases, it is shifting away from the mu null value (0). Because of the shift, the proportion of the times the null was rejected - power - increases towards 1.

### mu hat vs true mu and true mu (p < 0.05)

```{r}
mean_est =
  true_sim_df |> 
  group_by(true_mu) |> 
  summarize(
    avg_mu_hat = mean(estimate),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = true_mu, y = avg_mu_hat)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line()

mean_est

rj_mean_est =
  true_sim_df |> 
  filter(p.value < 0.05) |> 
  group_by(true_mu) |> 
  summarize(
    avg_mu_hat = mean(estimate),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = true_mu, y = avg_mu_hat)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line()

rj_mean_est
```

* The sample average of mu across tests is not approximately equal because the true value of mu depends on effect size and power (which is what was shown in mu vs power graph above). As true mu is closer to mu null (a smaller true mu) because are more likely to fail to reject the null. Those that reject the null (the one shown in the rj_mean_est plot) may end up inflating the estimate.
